paper_metadata.title: Hybrid Photonic Quantum Reservoir Computing for High-Dimensional Financial Surface Prediction

summary: The paper studies swaption surface prediction on 494 daily 14×16 surfaces using a hybrid photonic reservoir-computing pipeline. The main QORC + Ridge model uses 1,215 quantum features plus 120 classical features and achieves the best surface RMSE of 0.0425, while the best latent MSE is 0.0085 from the simpler single-reservoir ablation; the strongest classical baseline, Ridge Regression, reaches 0.0484 surface RMSE and 0.0091 latent MSE. Variational quantum baselines perform poorly, with VQC at R2 = -1.089 and Quantum LSTM at R2 = -1.306.

experiments.description: Fixed photonic quantum reservoir computing ensemble (three photonic reservoirs) combined with Ridge regression for next-day swaption surface prediction.

algorithm.variant: photonic quantum reservoir computing ensemble with fixed reservoirs and Ridge readout
algorithm.ansatz: fixed linear optical sandwich circuit U_rand · PS(phi) · U_rand
algorithm.optimizer: Ridge regression for readout; no trainable quantum optimizer
algorithm.convergence_criteria: closed-form Ridge solution; no iterative quantum training
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Haar-random unitary initialization for each reservoir; fixed after initialization

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 120-dimensional classical context projected to m modes via fixed orthogonal map, then sigmoid and phase encoding phi_i = 2pi * sigma(Wx); photonic Fock-basis probabilities used as features
problem_formulation.objective_function: predict next-day 20-dimensional latent code z_{t+1} from concatenated photonic features and classical temporal context; decoded to 224-dimensional swaption surface

problem_instance.description: Next-day prediction of 224-dimensional swaption surfaces from 494 daily trading days with 6 held-out future test days

dataset_specification.description: 14x16 tenor-maturity grid; training 439 windows, validation last 50 windows, test 6 future days

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: winsorization at 1st/99th percentiles on training data, robust scaling by median and IQR, min-max normalization to [0,1], sparse denoising autoencoder compression 224->20, temporal windowing with k=5 and first-difference momentum term
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: single held-out test set of 6 future trading days; metrics reported on latent MSE, surface RMSE, and R2

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: winsorization, robust scaling, min-max normalization, autoencoder compression, temporal windowing
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Ridge readout to latent code, decoder reconstruction to 224-dimensional surface

speedup_claims.caveats: Quantum feature extraction latency was excluded from reported inference time.
Reported latency excludes quantum feature extraction.
Reported latency excludes quantum feature extraction.
Reported latency excludes quantum feature extraction.

speedup_claims.conditions: photonic reservoir feature extraction; based on #P-hard permanents and combinatorial Fock-space growth
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper argues photonic hardware could enable feature extraction at optical speed, but all circuits were classically simulated and no asymptotic quantum advantage was demonstrated.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Fock-basis probability computation depends on permanents of unitary submatrices; classical simulation scales exponentially in photon number via combinatorial Fock-space size
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O((n+m-1 choose n)) for classical simulation of Fock probabilities
complexity_analysis.wall_clock_quantum: sub-millisecond inference reported for full model; quantum feature extraction excluded from reported latency

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Fixed photonic reservoir feature extraction with 3 reservoirs (12 modes/3 photons, 10 modes/4 photons, 16 modes/2 photons) plus closed-form Ridge readout; no trainable quantum parameters.
limiting_factors: Classical Ridge baseline is competitive and slightly worse on surface RMSE but better on latent MSE

notes: Hardware type inferred as real_qpu_photonic because the paper describes a photonic implementation and uses Perceval/MerLin, but it also states all circuits are classically simulated; no specific physical device name is given.
num_qubits is not explicitly stated because the paper reports photonic modes and photons rather than qubit registers; no gate-based qubit count is applicable.
Circuit depth is not reported for the photonic reservoir circuits.
Speedup claim is theoretical/qualitative only; no asymptotic quantum speedup over classical is established.
Authors report best surface RMSE (0.0425) but not a proven quantum advantage.
Classical Ridge achieves 0.0484 surface RMSE and 0.0091 latent MSE, so the quantum model is only partially better.
